source.title: CogEEGAgent: Toward Autonomous Cognitive EEG Analysis with Grounded Execution and Selection-Aware Verification

observations.text: CogEEGAgent cleanly separates semantic routing from scientific authority. In a prespecified 60-request routing benchmark, both the LLM router and matched FW-BM25 router share the same deterministic preflight. The LLM is exact on 39/40 valid unique requests versus 33/40 for FW-BM25, while the shared preflight produces the correct abstention on all 60/60 repeated required-abstention records and releases 0/60.

The deterministic boundary is explicitly stress-tested rather than inferred from final accuracy. Full preflight blocks all 200 internally inconsistent contract mutations, a source-frozen runtime matrix matches expected terminal state/executor-call/release behavior in 20/20 lifecycle cases, and a separate public-verifier matrix matches 188/188 hard-failure outcomes spanning scalar, cluster, no-call, malformed-value, contradiction, and evidence-binding cases.

CogEEGAgent also exposes the limit of deterministic validation: the same preflight accepts all 40/40 internally consistent wrong-template substitutions. Its single LLM routing error is likewise internally consistent and therefore released by preflight. This is direct science-domain evidence that contract consistency and safety authority cannot be treated as proof of semantic intent correctness.

The prospective release state machine treats model routes/prose as untrusted and makes release depend on contract validation, atomic commitment before confirmation opening, one-time confirmation access, typed finite evidence, independent replay, evidence/hash binding, falsification, and source-frozen scorer acceptance. Failed schema/objective/hash/replay/transition guards terminate in Abstained rather than Released.

In the 21-request externally model-authored composed campaign, 12 guarded preflight hazards release 0 reports and three post-release reuse/retry requests release 0; only the three supported analyses release. Three underspecified requests are routed incorrectly by the LLM but lifecycle enforcement still prevents report release, illustrating containment distinct from semantic correctness.

The selection-aware scientific confirmation experiment isolates policy from the LLM/registry. Uncorrected best-p search has 16.5% false-positive rate, while participant-disjoint held-out confirmation reduces it to 4.9% (reported reduction 11.6 points, 95% subject-cluster CI 11.0-12.1). This is outcome-bearing evidence that evidence-release authority should be bound to a prespecified confirmation policy rather than adaptive search alone.

protocol_inferences.name: DETERMINISTIC_PREFLIGHT_OWNS_ADMISSIBILITY_NOT_SEMANTIC_TRUTH
protocol_inferences.text: A deterministic preflight can own fail-closed admissibility and exact lifecycle transitions, but semantic routing correctness remains a separate claim. A packet that is internally valid must not thereby be labeled semantically correct.

protocol_inferences.name: RELEASE_STATE_MUST_BE_DERIVED_FROM_EVIDENCE_BOUND_TRANSITIONS
protocol_inferences.text: Scientific completion/release should be derived from typed evidence, immutable commitment, freshness/partition constraints, independent replay, and deterministic transition checks; model prose or self-verification cannot directly write Released.

protocol_inferences.name: SEMANTIC_ERROR_CONTAINMENT_IS_DISTINCT_FROM_SEMANTIC_ERROR_PREVENTION
protocol_inferences.text: When semantic fit cannot be deterministically adjudicated, the control plane should at least prevent unsupported evidence release or forbidden lifecycle reuse. Containment success must be reported separately from route correctness.

protocol_inferences.name: ADAPTIVE_SELECTION_REQUIRES_CONFIRMATION_BOUND_RELEASE
protocol_inferences.text: Evidence selected adaptively should not inherit release authority merely because it is numerically valid; bind release to a prespecified correction or disjoint confirmation resource, with the selected candidate committed before confirmation is opened.

phase1_acceptance.reason: CogEEGAgent supplies strong scientific control-plane evidence, but its demonstrated end-to-end path depends on deterministic scientific executors, EEG data access, model routing and independent replay. It is not a zero-external-executor scheduled-Chat parity solution.

scope_notes: Do not claim deterministic preflight resolves semantic intent; the paper deliberately demonstrates 40/40 internally consistent wrong-template releases.
Do not claim held-out confirmation is universally optimal; the paper states max-T is preferable when the complete adaptive search is trustworthy and replayable.
Use the source as science-domain evidence for authority separation, abstention, lifecycle containment and evidence-bound release, not as an end-to-end Phase-1 acceptance route.
